title: NRF2 activation resolves neuropathic pain via dual antioxidant and Na(V)1.7-Suppressive mechanisms.
authors: Shan, Zhiming; Cai, Song; Yang, Haoyi; Guo, Weijie; Wu, Chaoran; Cheung, Martin; Luo, Xin; Cheung, Chi Wai; Liu, Jessica Aijia
journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
one_liner_zh: 该文研究NRF2激活通过抗氧化和抑制Na(V)1.7通道缓解神经病理性疼痛，属于神经科学/疼痛药理领域，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Neuropathic pain remains a major clinical challenge, with current analgesics often proving ineffective and frequently refractory. Nociceptive responses are protective, while dysregulation of pain-resolving mechanisms drives the pain to be pathological. Enhancing resolving and protective signaling pathways is critical for treating neuropathic pain, yet such knowledge remains limited. In this study, we revealed the antinociceptive effects of Nrf2 in sensory neurons under both physiological and pathological conditions. Notably, insufficient activation of endogenous Nrf2 underlies the transition from acute to chronic neuropathic pain, while its activation exerts dual therapeutic effects: (1) ameliorating oxidative stress induced by peripheral nerve injury, and (2) specifically inhibiting the pathological increased Na(V)1.7 current density. Na(V)1.7 is a sodium channel with its well-established role in promoting nociceptive amplification and transmission but has failed in clinical trials by direct targeting inhibitors due to poor pharmacokinetics. Mechanistically, Nrf2 transcriptionally activated E3 ubiquitin ligase Nedd4-2, promoting Na(V)1.7 endocytosis, thereby suppressing pathological nociceptive transmission. Through combined network pharmacology screening and in silico molecular docking, we identified two NRF2-activating compounds-echinacoside and artesunate-that leverage this dual mechanism to achieve superior analgesic efficacy. These findings address critical limitations of current neuropathic pain treatments by activating new pain-resolving and protective pathways with immediate translational potential.
abstract_zh: 神经病理性疼痛仍然是临床上的重大挑战，现有镇痛药往往效果不佳且常呈难治性。伤害性反应具有保护性，而疼痛消退机制失调则使疼痛转为病理性。增强消退性和保护性信号通路对治疗神经病理性疼痛至关重要，但此类知识仍十分有限。在本研究中，我们揭示了Nrf2在感觉神经元中在生理和病理条件下的抗伤害性效应。值得注意的是，内源性Nrf2激活不足是急性向慢性神经病理性疼痛转变的基础，而其激活发挥双重治疗作用：（1）改善外周神经损伤诱导的氧化应激，（2）特异性抑制病理性增加的Na(V)1.7电流密度。Na(V)1.7是一种钠通道，其在促进伤害性放大和传递中的作用已明确，但直接靶向抑制剂因药代动力学不佳而在临床试验中失败。机制上，Nrf2转录激活E3泛素连接酶Nedd4-2，促进Na(V)1.7内吞，从而抑制病理性伤害性传递。通过结合网络药理学筛选和计算机分子对接，我们鉴定了两种Nrf2激活化合物——松果菊苷和青蒿琥酯——它们利用这一双重机制实现优越的镇痛效果。这些发现通过激活新的疼痛消退和保护性通路，解决了当前神经病理性疼痛治疗的关键局限性，并具有即时转化潜力。
